source_title: Staffline Group Annual Report and Accounts 2019
availability_evidence: Annual report pages 27 and 61 state that the report and financial statements were approved and authorised for issue by the Board on 29 June 2020; issuer-hosted report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Revenue fell 3.9% to £1,076.7m, gross profit 25.9% to £86.5m and gross margin from 10.4% to 8.0%, while underlying operating profit reversed from £32.8m to a £0.8m loss and the reported pretax loss widened to £48.1m. Net debt remained £67.9m post-IFRS 16, facilities required restructuring, covenant waivers and extensions, and the report described material Covid uncertainty. Prior-period errors, deliberate report manipulation, goodwill impairment and control failures compounded the pressure, though pre-IFRS 16 debt declined slightly and renewed facilities supported going concern.
already_announced_exclusion: The Recruitment GB reorganisation, PeoplePlus transformation and Work Programme wind-down, June 2020 credit-facility restructuring, covenant waivers, governance and control remediation, Board and finance leadership changes and announced Covid measures are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Losses, severe margin contraction, weak trading, financing dependence, covenant intervention, control failures and pandemic uncertainty create extreme pressure. Slightly lower pre-IFRS 16 debt and completed financing support offer only limited contrary evidence.

source_title: Staffline Group Annual Report and Accounts 2021
availability_evidence: Annual report pages 83 and 85 state that the financial statements were approved and authorised for issue by the Board on 21 March 2022; issuer-hosted report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Revenue rose 1.6% to £942.7m, gross profit 11% to £82.8m and underlying operating profit 114.6% to £10.3m, with the Group returning to statutory profit. A £46.4m equity raise and debt refinancing transformed pre-IFRS 16 net debt of £8.8m into net cash of £6.9m, with significant facility headroom. The comprehensive restructuring and turnaround were declared successfully complete, while profitability, cash flow and early-2022 trading exceeded expectations despite labour, supply-chain and Covid disruption.
already_announced_exclusion: The completed Group restructuring and turnaround, headcount reduction, property rationalisation, PeoplePlus alignment, lower-margin contract exits, governance strengthening, June 2021 refinancing and equity raise are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Residual labour, supply-chain and pandemic uncertainty create limited pressure. Strong profit and gross-profit growth, positive net cash, facility headroom and explicit completion of the turnaround provide exceptionally strong contrary evidence.

source_title: Staffline Group Annual Report and Accounts 2023
availability_evidence: Annual report pages 111 and 113 state that the financial statements were approved and authorised for issue by the Board on 18 March 2024; issuer-hosted report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Revenue rose 1.1% to £938.2m but gross profit fell 1.5% to £80.8m, underlying EBITDA 13.6% to £15.2m and underlying operating profit 14.2% to £10.3m. The Group reported an £11.0m statutory loss after PeoplePlus impairment and restructuring charges. Cash performance exceeded expectations and pre-IFRS 16 net cash remained £3.8m after a £5m buyback, while Recruitment GB gained share and second-half revenue improved despite weak demand and macroeconomic pressure.
already_announced_exclusion: The Recruitment GB cost-base programme, PeoplePlus restructuring and exit from in-person skills, disclosed redundancies and overhead reductions, £8.9m goodwill impairment and completed £5m share buyback are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Underlying earnings and gross profit contraction, a statutory loss, weak demand and substantial divisional restructuring create moderate pressure. Positive cash, market-share gains, second-half improvement, performance ahead of expectations and a strong balance sheet provide substantial offsets.
